result.summary: Do not ship: the new binding turns plain-text error content into injected HTML.

findings.title: Notification HTML injection permits deceptive links
findings.body: Adding the autoqueue pattern `Reconnect account` twice produces a concrete injection: AutoQueueService.add embeds the duplicate pattern in its error message, settings-page.component.ts:236–241 passes that message unchanged to NotificationService, and this binding renders a clickable external link instead of literal text. Angular's sanitizer explicitly allows anchors and HTTPS hrefs; it does not preserve the removed text-only protection. This also misrenders legitimate patterns containing markup. The existing bell tests override the template with the old interpolation, so they cannot catch this regression.
findings.recommendation: Restore text interpolation. If notifications need links, represent those as separate validated fields and render explicit template anchors. Test markup-containing errors against the actual component template.

next_steps: Restore text-only rendering and add a regression test for duplicate patterns containing HTML.
